rows.description: Each member of a college team quietly thinks he did most of the work, so shares add up to well over the whole. Fair recognition needs written records.

rows.description: A grounded professional names what she did well, what luck helped and what she got wrong, and thanks others honestly. Balanced credit builds trust and learning.

rows.description: A child says he pushed because he was hurried but says the other child pushed because he is rude. His own acts have reasons; others' have character.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager explains his own shouting as stress and the parent's as anger and control, while the parent thinks the opposite. Each sees the other's situation poorly.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student in conflict describes the incident as if it were happening to a friend, then from the other person's seat, and finds the situational reasons on both sides.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A manager blames a late employee's attitude while she would blame traffic for herself. Noticing the double standard makes feedback fairer and more curious.

rows.subtype: It will not happen to me [Actor]
rows.description: A child is sure he will not get caught, fall from the tree or fail the test. Bad outcomes seem to happen to other people.

rows.description: A teenager riding without a helmet or vaping believes the harm is for others. Feeling invulnerable is partly developmental, since the brain weighs immediate reward heavily.

rows.description: A graduate expects the first job, savings and relationship to go better than average and skips backup plans. Hope is healthy but unprepared hope is fragile.

rows.description: A wise planner keeps optimism for effort but adds a buffer, an emergency fund and a plan B, so setbacks bother her plan and not her sense of self.
